items.item: A job is spawned by one action and scoped to that action, never to the DataFrame or the data: calling the same action twice on unchanged data produces two distinct job ids.
A stage's task count equals its partition count, not the row count or data size — repartitioning without changing the data changes only the task count.

The driver is the one process holding the whole job's coordinating state (the SparkContext); losing it ends the application, while losing one executor only loses that executor's tasks, which get rescheduled elsewhere.
An executor's slot count (its real concurrency) is its core count; an application's total task parallelism across the cluster is cores per executor times the number of executors granted.

items.item: Local mode (`local[N]`) runs the driver and N executor-equivalent worker threads in a single JVM; it exercises the real DAGScheduler/TaskScheduler job-stage-task counting but cannot demonstrate independent-process executor failure.

items.item: Spark Connect decouples where client code runs from where the driver runs (a thin client submits an unresolved plan over gRPC to a server-side driver), without changing the job/stage/task accounting this topic measures.

A stage boundary exists specifically where a shuffle is required; this refresher names the boundary's existence and hands its precise cut rule (narrow vs. wide dependencies) to the next topic rather than re-deriving it here.

items.item: spark.default.parallelism and spark.sql.shuffle.partitions are two distinct settings governing different operations' default partition counts, not interchangeable; this refresher's repartition(8) example sets the count explicitly rather than relying on either default.

at.out: de.task-scheduling-locality-parallelism teaches the two settings' distinction precisely

items.item: Dynamic allocation lets an application's executor count grow and shrink during a run rather than staying fixed at submission; this refresher's local[4] run uses a fixed executor-equivalent count throughout.

at.out: named only as a boundary; dynamic allocation's mechanics are not this refresher's scope
